headline: Brockton adult foster-care provider agrees to $1.25M MassHealth settlement
dek: WeCare 365 will pay MassHealth and adopt new compliance measures to resolve allegations that caregiver logs did not properly document services provided to members, the Massachusetts attorney general said.
body: WeCare 365, an adult foster-care provider in Brockton, has agreed to pay $1.25 million to MassHealth to resolve allegations that it failed to maintain proper caregiver logs documenting services provided to members, Massachusetts Attorney General Andrea Joy Campbell announced Monday.

The settlement also requires the provider to spend $200,000 enhancing its electronic medical-record system, review all caregiver logs monthly and create a training program for new employees on adult foster-care rules. WeCare 365 must also contract with a reporting system that allows people to report suspected fraud anonymously.

The attorney general's announcement described the matter as a regulatory settlement based on allegations. Campbell's office said the case was handled by its Medicaid Fraud Division, which investigates suspected fraud involving MassHealth and can also pursue abuse, neglect and financial-exploitation complaints involving Medicaid patients and long-term-care residents.

The announcement comes as the office continues to scrutinize public-funded health-care providers. The attorney general said the division previously secured guilty pleas in 2025 involving separate Massachusetts home-health and adult foster-care fraud cases.

Under the agreement, the payment will go back to MassHealth while the compliance measures are intended to improve documentation and oversight for future adult foster-care services, according to the attorney general's office.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Brockton provider agrees to $1.25M MassHealth settlement
seoDescription: WeCare 365 will pay $1.25 million to MassHealth and add compliance measures under a settlement announced by Massachusetts Attorney General Andrea Campbell.
